items.followUp: A force of 120 N acts on a 15 kg body initially at rest. Find the distance through which it acts to give the body a speed of 40 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Newton’s second law gives an acceleration of 10 m s⁻².
rubric.description: Finds the acceleration from the applied force and mass.
rubric.how: Award for calculating a = F/m = 10 m s⁻².

rubric.why: This equation relates the initial velocity, final velocity, acceleration and distance.
rubric.description: Selects the appropriate equation of motion.
rubric.how: Award for writing the equation used to find the distance.

rubric.why: Substitution of the given values leads to 2500 = 20s.
rubric.description: Substitutes the velocities and acceleration correctly.
rubric.how: Award for correct substitution into the equation of motion.

rubric.why: Solving the equation gives a distance of 125 m.
rubric.description: Calculates and states the distance through which the force acts.
rubric.how: Award for the correct distance with its unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F = 200 N, m = 20 kg, u = 0 m s⁻¹, v = 50 m s⁻¹.
Substitution: a = (200 N)/(20 kg) = 10 m s⁻².
Substitution: (50 m s⁻¹)² = (0 m s⁻¹)² + 2(10 m s⁻²)s.
Distance: s = 2500 m² s⁻² ÷ 20 m s⁻² = 125 m.
